# Prism

> Inspect the evidence behind a WebMCP contract.

Prism compares expected names with supplied tool snapshots. It checks schema shape, annotations, reported outcomes, runtime observations, and reported approval preservation. It does not independently verify semantic task completion or certify safety. Examples are synthetic and remain labeled as examples.

- App: https://prism.alx21.chatgpt.site/
- Source and full guide: https://github.com/agammann/prism-webmcp
- Optional companion: https://prism.alx21.chatgpt.site/prism-webmcp-companion.zip

## Page-owned WebMCP tools

- get_evaluation_context (read, {}): reads current draft including actual custom fields and source selection.
- choose_evaluation_profile (write, {profile}): changes draft contract; preserves JSON and marks previous report stale.
- run_sample_evaluation (write, {profile}): evaluates a synthetic example. Custom uses the current custom fields.
- evaluate_current_snapshot (write, {}): evaluates the entered JSON against the current contract. Requires Runner snapshot mode.
- get_latest_evaluation (read, {}): reads the report with its exact contract, target, source, findings, and stale flag.

Profiles: commerce, operations, editor, custom. Inputs are strict; extra properties are rejected. Tools use document.modelContext.registerTool with lifecycle cleanup. Registration status appears in the Agent activity panel. Manual controls work without native WebMCP.

## Data and evidence

JSON analysis happens in the browser; Prism does not visit target labels. Imports and reports live in tab memory. Save reports using Download report JSON, and keep the original snapshot separately. Changing the setup does not silently alter the previous report.

The optional companion uses activeTab and scripting. Unknown or mutating tools require a fresh confirmation. It exports descriptors, schemas, contract text, origin/path, hashes, timestamps, and outcome flags. Raw inputs, outputs, errors, expected text, and URL query/fragment are omitted. Review descriptors and paths before sharing. DOM differences and substring matches are limited observations, not semantic proof.
